summary: 60-foot steel lookout on the Cape Romain refuge in Charleston County, SC; the register says it is abandoned after two legs collapsed in June 2014.

facts.status_note: Two legs collapsed around June 14, 2014, after years of rust; the Register describes the tower as abandoned.

events.note: NHLR build year; the description says built in the 1930s
Registered April 7, 2011 as US 906, SC 9; nominated by Ron Stafford
Two legs collapsed around June 14, 2014, after years of rust

evidence.supports: 60-foot steel tower beside the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway; now abandoned
evidence.quote: Built in the 1930s, this 60' steel tower located on the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway is now abandoned.

evidence.supports: on the Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge
administered by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service
after years of rust, two legs collapsed around June 14, 2014
evidence.quote: After years of rust, two of its legs collapsed on about June 14, 2014.

evidence.supports: also filed under the name Horsehead Creek

corrections.why: The Register describes the tower as abandoned and says two of its legs collapsed about June 14, 2014.

notes_for_editor: One substantive source (NHLR). The Forest Lookouts page has only a header (Charleston County; spelled 'Cape Romaine Wildlife Refuge' there, 'Cape Romain' in NHLR; the story uses NHLR's spelling). The record's status 'standing' is contradicted by NHLR (abandoned, legs collapsed June 2014), so a correction is proposed for human review. Height 60 ft converted to 18.3 m (structure height, not cab). No source gives access, staffing, or condition since 2014, so no access or visit facts are recorded. One web search for removal or collapse news found nothing relevant. The record's June 2014 downed-tower photo was not re-read. No new photos added.
